subject: Confirming authoritative SOC 2 package and bridge letter for procurement
body:
--- Original message ---
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II package — procurement needs current artifacts

Hi Marissa,

We are in the final stages of procurement for AcmeCorp and need the authoritative SOC 2 Type II artifacts to satisfy our internal auditors. The copy we currently have in vendor onboarding is labeled SOC2-2021-RED-01 and shows an audit period that ended 2024-04-30 — our security team flagged it as expired.

Can you send the latest official package (report, bridge/interim letter if applicable, and evidence index) that we should accept? Also, if there was a reissue with a new report id or a superseding package please call that out — procurement needs to know which file supersedes the older one.

Target: legal needs to approve by Friday.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Vendor Risk Manager | AcmeCorp


--- Reply ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II package — procurement needs current artifacts

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the deadline.

Short answer: we do have a reissued package; we want to make sure procurement accepts the reissue as the authoritative artifact. A little context so your security/legal folks can triage quickly:

- Previous package id: SOC2-2021-RED-01 (audit period 2023-05-01 through 2024-04-30) — this is the file you have and which procurement flagged as expired.
- Reissue: SOC2-2026-RDWD-V2 (reissued June 2027) — this contains the same coverage window extended by the auditor's interim procedures and includes an updated evidence index.
- We also have a signed bridge letter covering continuity between the two audit periods; legal typically accepts the reissued package + bridge when the audit firm issues a reissue that supersedes the prior package.

Soojin (CC) — can you confirm whether the reissue formally supersedes the earlier report id, and whether we should send the full reissue bundle plus bridge or send a short cover note + bridge first?

If helpful, I can send the reissued bundle and the bridge letter via secure link.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192


--- Internal note (marissa -> soojin, neha) ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: FW: AcmeCorp procurement — which artifact to send?

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Quick facts: auditor reissued a package in June 2027 (id SOC2-2026-RDWD-V2). Legal said the reissue supersedes SOC2-2021-RED-01, but procurement teams sometimes reject reissues if they don't see an explicit "supersedes" statement or a signed bridge attesting continuity.

Questions for legal/compliance:
- Is the June 2027 reissued bundle the "authoritative" artifact that procurement should accept unilaterally?
- Do we need to provide both the reissue zip and a separate bridge letter signed by the auditor? (my read: send both to avoid back-and-forth)
- Any special text we should include in a cover email that procurement expects (e.g., explicit reference to original report id and the audit-period continuity)?

Neha — can you weigh in? If we can confirm that the reissue supersedes and a one-page signed bridge is sufficient, I'll send both and include a HubSpot note linking the DocuSign for signature.

Quoted below is Samir's original message for context.

Thanks,
Marissa


--- Final reply to AcmeCorp (sent) ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmecorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II package — procurement needs current artifacts

Hi Samir / Procurement team —

Per our internal compliance/legal review, please find the authoritative materials below. We are sending the reissued package plus a signed bridge letter to make the acceptance path as clear as possible.

Attachments (stubs):
- SOC2_Redwood_2026_Reissue.zip (zip, 22MB) — full reissued Type II bundle, auditor cover letter, control testing summaries, and updated evidence index.
- bridge_letter_2027-08-25.pdf (pdf, 45KB) — signed bridge attestation from Redwood's auditor confirming continuity and explaining the reissue relationship to SOC2-2021-RED-01.

Key points to include in your review:
- Authoritative report id: SOC2-2026-RDWD-V2 (reissued June 2027). This package supersedes SOC2-2021-RED-01 for the purposes of vendor assessment.
- Audit coverage: continuity maintained; effective coverage for control testing reflected through 2026-04-30 per the auditor's addendum.
- If your security or legal team requires a DocuSign-signed acceptance or a short cover attestation from Redwood, we have a DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.com/intl/en/link/to/bridge-attestation/abc123

Next steps: please confirm receipt and let me know if the reissued package + bridge letter satisfies AcmeCorp's procurement team. If you need the original report id included as an appendix in the procurement packet, we can include a short "lineage" paragraph.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with your legal lead if helpful.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
